features.title: Sign up with email and password
acceptance: POST /auth/sign-up with {"email": "  Me+<ts>@Example.com ", "password": "correct-horse"}: 201, body {user: {id, email, created_at}, token}; user.email is "me+<ts>@example.com"; token is a base64url string of at least 43 chars
Repeat the same sign-up (any letter case): 409 with error.code "email_taken"
POST /auth/sign-up with email "not-an-email": 400, error.code "validation_error", error.message mentions "email"
POST /auth/sign-up with a 7-char password, then with a 129-char password: both 400 "validation_error" naming "password"
POST /auth/sign-up with a body that is not valid JSON: 400 "validation_error"
Every error body has the shape {error: {code, message}}; no response ever contains the password or a password hash

In Postgres (DATABASE_URL from .env.test, via psql): the tokens row holds a 64-char hex SHA-256 of the returned token, never the token itself; the users row holds an scrypt hash and a salt, never the password

features.title: Sign in returns a new token
acceptance: Sign up as a fresh email, then POST /auth/sign-in with the same email (in upper case) and password: 200 {user, token}; the token differs from the sign-up token
POST /auth/sign-in with the right email and a wrong password: 401 error.code "invalid_credentials"
POST /auth/sign-in with an email that was never signed up: 401 with exactly the same code and message as the wrong-password case
POST /auth/sign-in without a password: 400 "validation_error" naming "password"

features.title: Who am I: GET /me with a bearer token
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
GET /me with the sign-up token: 200 {id, email, created_at} matching the sign-up user
GET /me without an Authorization header: 401 error.code "unauthorized"
GET /me with `Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token`: 401 "unauthorized"
GET /me with a token of a second user returns that user's email, not the first one's

features.title: Sign out revokes only the token used
acceptance: Sign up (token A), then sign in with the same account (token B)
POST /auth/sign-out with token A: 204 with an empty body
GET /me with token A: 401 "unauthorized"; POST /auth/sign-out with token A again: 401
GET /me with token B: still 200
POST /auth/sign-out without a token: 401 "unauthorized"

features.title: Unknown routes use the error envelope
acceptance: GET /no-such-route: 404 with body {error: {code: "not_found", message}}
POST /no-such-route with a JSON body: 404 "not_found" with the same shape
GET /openapi.json: 200 without a token

features.title: Save a bookmark
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
POST /bookmarks {"url": " https://example.com/a "}: 201 with {id, url: "https://example.com/a", title: "https://example.com/a", note: null, read_at: null, tags: [], created_at, updated_at}
POST /bookmarks {"url": "https://example.com/b", "title": "B", "note": "why"}: 201 with that title and note
POST /bookmarks with url "ftp://x.y", with "not a url", with a relative "/path", and with no url: each 400 "validation_error" naming "url"
POST /bookmarks with a 2049-char url, a 501-char title, a 10,001-char note: each 400 naming the field
POST /bookmarks without a token: 401 "unauthorized"

features.title: Duplicate url is rejected with the existing id
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
POST /bookmarks {url: "https://example.com/dup"}: 201, note its id
POST /bookmarks {url: "  https://example.com/dup  "}: 409 error.code "duplicate_url" and error.existing_id equals the first id
POST /bookmarks {url: "https://example.com/dup/"}: 201 (different string, no normalization)
A second user saving "https://example.com/dup": 201 (duplicates are per user)

features.title: Get one bookmark by id
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save a bookmark, then GET /bookmarks/<id>: 200 with the same bookmark
As a second user, GET /bookmarks/<first user's id>: 404 "not_found" (not 403)
GET /bookmarks/<random uuid> and GET /bookmarks/not-a-uuid: both 404 "not_found"
GET /bookmarks/<id> without a token: 401

features.title: List my bookmarks with cursor pagination
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
As a fresh user with no bookmarks, GET /bookmarks: 200 {items: [], next_cursor: null}
Save three bookmarks A, B, C in that order; GET /bookmarks?limit=2: items [C, B] and a non-null next_cursor
GET /bookmarks?limit=2&cursor=<next_cursor>: items [A], next_cursor null
GET /bookmarks: all three, newest first (default limit 20); a second user's bookmarks never appear
GET /bookmarks?limit=0 and ?limit=101 and ?limit=abc: 400 "validation_error" naming "limit"
GET /bookmarks?cursor=garbage and with a next_cursor whose characters were changed: 400 "invalid_cursor"

features.title: Edit a bookmark's title and note
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save a bookmark with a note; PATCH /bookmarks/<id> {"title": "New"}: 200, title "New", note unchanged, updated_at later than before
PATCH /bookmarks/<id> {"note": null}: 200 with note null
PATCH /bookmarks/<id> {"title": ""}: 400 "validation_error" naming "title"
PATCH /bookmarks/<id> {"url": "https://other.example"}: the url stays the original
PATCH another user's bookmark id: 404 "not_found"; without a token: 401

features.title: Delete a bookmark
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save a bookmark; DELETE /bookmarks/<id>: 204; then GET /bookmarks/<id>: 404
DELETE the same id again: 404 "not_found"
DELETE another user's bookmark id: 404, and that bookmark still exists for its owner
The url can be saved again after deletion: POST it again gives 201

features.title: Mark a bookmark read
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save a bookmark; PUT /bookmarks/<id>/read: 200 with read_at set to a timestamp
PUT /bookmarks/<id>/read again: 200 with the same read_at as the first time
PUT /bookmarks/<another user's id>/read: 404; without a token: 401

features.title: Mark a bookmark unread
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save and mark read a bookmark; DELETE /bookmarks/<id>/read: 200 with read_at null
DELETE /bookmarks/<id>/read on an unread bookmark: 200 with read_at null
DELETE /bookmarks/<another user's id>/read: 404; without a token: 401

features.title: Filter bookmarks by read status
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save three bookmarks and mark the middle one read
GET /bookmarks?status=read: only the read one; GET /bookmarks?status=unread: the other two, newest first
GET /bookmarks?status=unread&limit=1: one item and a next_cursor; following it returns the other unread one and next_cursor null
GET /bookmarks?status=done: 400 "validation_error" naming "status"

features.title: Contract documents every route, status and error body
acceptance: GET /openapi.json: every M1 route is listed
Every protected route documents 401, every route with an :id documents 404, every route with a body or query documents 400, all with the {error: {code, message}} schema
POST /bookmarks documents 409 with existing_id; POST /auth/sign-up documents 409
A test fails when a route is added without these error responses

features.title: Latency budget for listing bookmarks with 1,000 bookmarks
acceptance: `npm run perf` seeds a user with 1,000 bookmarks (some read) and loads GET /bookmarks, GET /bookmarks?limit=100, GET /bookmarks?status=read and a cursor page with that user's token
Each has p99 under 150 ms locally and the run fails when one goes over

features.title: Tag a bookmark
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save a bookmark; PUT /bookmarks/<id>/tags/Reading: 200 with tags ["reading"]
PUT the same tag again: 200, tags still ["reading"] (idempotent)
PUT /bookmarks/<id>/tags/bad_tag and a 33-char tag: 400 "validation_error" naming "tag"
Add 10 different tags, then an 11th: 400 "too_many_tags"; re-adding one of the 10 is still 200
GET /bookmarks/<id> shows the tags sorted by name; another user's id gives 404; no token gives 401

features.title: Remove a tag from a bookmark
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Tag a bookmark "a" and "b"; DELETE /bookmarks/<id>/tags/a: 200 with tags ["b"]
DELETE /bookmarks/<id>/tags/a again: 200, tags ["b"] (idempotent)
DELETE on another user's bookmark: 404; without a token: 401

features.title: List my tags with counts
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
As a fresh user, GET /tags: 200 {items: []}
Tag two bookmarks "read-later" and one of them also "go"; GET /tags: {items: [{name: "go", count: 1}, {name: "read-later", count: 2}]}
Remove "go" from its bookmark; GET /tags no longer lists "go"
A second user's tags never appear; without a token: 401

features.title: Rename a tag, merging into an existing one
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Tag bookmark 1 "js"; PATCH /tags/js {"name": "JavaScript"}: 200 {name: "javascript", count: 1}; bookmark 1 now has "javascript"
Tag bookmark 2 "ts" and "web", bookmark 3 "web"; PATCH /tags/ts {"name": "web"}: 200 {name: "web", count: 2}; bookmark 2 has "web" once and no "ts"
A bookmark with 10 tags renamed into one it already has keeps 9 tags (no 400)
PATCH /tags/unknown {"name": "x"}: 404 "not_found"; PATCH with an invalid new name: 400 naming "name"
Renaming never changes a second user's tags; without a token: 401

features.title: Filter bookmarks by tag
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save three bookmarks, tag two "go", mark one of those read
GET /bookmarks?tag=go: the two, newest first; GET /bookmarks?tag=Go gives the same
GET /bookmarks?tag=go&status=unread: only the unread one
GET /bookmarks?tag=go&limit=1 then follow next_cursor: the second one, then next_cursor null
GET /bookmarks?tag=nope: {items: [], next_cursor: null}; ?tag=bad_tag: 400 naming "tag"

features.title: Search bookmarks by text
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Save A {title: "Rust book"}, B {url: "https://go.dev/doc"}, C {note: "zebra migration notes"}
GET /bookmarks?q=zebra: only C; ?q=rust: only A; ?q=go.dev: B
Tag C "x" and mark it read; ?q=zebra&tag=x&status=read: C; ?q=zebra&status=unread: empty
?q=notes&limit=1 with two matching bookmarks: newest first, and next_cursor reaches the second
?q= (empty): same as no q; another user's matching bookmarks never appear

features.title: Write rate limit per token
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Send 60 POST /bookmarks within one minute with one token: all 201 or 409
The 61st write (POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE) in the same minute: 429 error.code "rate_limited" with a Retry-After header of 1 to 60 seconds
Another token of the same user (from sign-in) can still write in that minute
After waiting Retry-After seconds, the first token can write again
GET /bookmarks with the limited token still works (reads count separately)

features.title: Read rate limit per token
acceptance: Use a fresh email per run, e.g. `me+<timestamp>@example.com`, and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from sign-up
Send 300 GET /bookmarks within one minute with one token: all 200
The 301st GET in the same minute: 429 "rate_limited" with Retry-After
GET /openapi.json is never limited

features.title: Sign-in attempt limit per email
acceptance: Sign up a fresh email; make 10 POST /auth/sign-in attempts within 15 minutes (mix of right and wrong passwords): each 200 or 401
The 11th attempt, even with the right password and the email in different case: 429 "rate_limited" with a Retry-After header
Sign-in for a different email still works; POST /auth/sign-up is never limited

features.title: Latency budget for tag filter, search and tag list
acceptance: `npm run perf` also loads GET /bookmarks?tag=<tag>, GET /bookmarks?q=<word>, GET /bookmarks?q=<word>&tag=<tag>&status=unread and GET /tags for a user with 1,000 tagged bookmarks
Each has p99 under 150 ms locally and the run fails when one goes over

features.title: Contract covers tags, search and rate limits
acceptance: GET /openapi.json lists every M2 route with its 400, 401 and 404 errors
Every rate-limited route documents 429 with the Retry-After header; GET /bookmarks documents the tag, status and q query params
The contract coverage test from F015 passes for all routes
